boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the sole frozen record in the Fredericksburg Campaign. Preserve the December 11–15, 1862 interval; the live NPS campaign heading does not replace it. Opening personnel and exact effective command boundaries remain unresolved. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. Imported numerical estimates remain unchanged; this pass does not validate them as simultaneous opening forces.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads 172,504 total (US 100,007; CS 72,497). The live NPS field reads 100007 total (US 0; CS 100007;), assigning the Union figure to the Confederate side. Palfrey gives about 113,000 Union present for duty from Burnside's report of December 13, upward of 78,000 Confederate from Lee's report of December 10, and 127,574 Union present for duty on November 10.
claims.rationale: Frozen, live and reported present-for-duty figures differ in scope and date; the live side assignment is not adopted. None is a matched opening population; present-for-duty is not engaged strength.

claims.value: Palfrey describes a shoulder-high stone wall with earth piled against it along the road below Marye's, forming a nearly perfect infantry parapet with guns and sharpshooters firing over it; he calls the Confederate position strong by nature and strengthened by art. NPS says Lee entrenched on the heights behind the town.
claims.rationale: Position and works description; no map verification or numerical terrain effect. The works were prepared before the interval by the defending commander.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 17,929 total (US 13,353; CS 4,576); the live NPS field reads 17900 total (US 12600; CS 5300;). Palfrey prints Burnside's reported losses by grand division, totalling 1,180 killed, 9,028 wounded and 2,145 missing (which sum to 12,353), and Confederate losses of 1,894 for Longstreet's corps over five days and 3,415 for Jackson's.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. The sum of Palfrey's Union columns is computed here, not printed; Longstreet's figure spans five days.

open_questions: Original returns, orders to Franklin, Hardie's despatches and casualty reconciliation remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family; Palfrey is one retrospective history by a former colonel of the 20th Massachusetts who says he drew on his own recollection and used advance sheets of the Official Records; his service in this campaign is not shown in the inspected text. Reports and writers quoted or summarized inside Palfrey are not additional independently inspected families.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
